bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42488143 (fluent-bit): Heap-use-after-free READ 8 found by fuzz target flb-it-fuzz-parser_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ [asan].
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The staged 100-byte parser_fuzzer witness makes the harness select `format = "logfmt"`, create a non-null 15-byte `time_fmt`, create a non-null 15-byte `time_offset` string `"\xff              "`, omit `time_key` and `types`, and allocate a one-element decoder `mk_list`. `flb_parser_create()` stores that caller-owned list in `p->decoders` before creation succeeds. Because `time_fmt` is present, parser creation later validates `time_offset`; `flb_parser_tzone_offset()` rejects the leading `0xFF` and returns `-1`. Vulnerable `flb_parser_create()` then unwinds with `flb_parser_destroy(p)`, which frees `p->decoders` even though creation failed and ownership of `list` never transferred. The harness still enters its `fuzz_parser == NULL` cleanup branch and calls `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` again. That second destroy immediately iterates the freed 16-byte list head at `src/flb_parser_decoder.c:743`, producing the observed ASan heap-use-after-free READ of size 8. The fix replaces these create-time `flb_parser_destroy(p)` calls with `flb_interim_parser_destroy(p)` so caller-owned `decoders` and `types` are left untouched on failure.

source.description: Source. Parser creation imports the attacker-controlled decoder-list pointer from the harness into project state by storing caller-owned `decoders` in `p->decoders` before creation has succeeded.
source.value_from: The staged witness enables the decoder-list branch in `parser_fuzzer.c`, which allocates one `struct mk_list` decoder list and passes that pointer as the `decoders` argument to `flb_parser_create()`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The second `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` starts iterating a list head that was already freed during the create-time unwind, so the loop reads stale list pointers and triggers the heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 reported at line 743.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free` in `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy /src/fluent-bit/src/flb_parser_decoder.c:743:5`, with the same 16-byte region previously freed from line 761 during the earlier destroy.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On a create-time `time_offset` parse failure, vulnerable `flb_parser_create()` unwinds with the full `flb_parser_destroy(p)` even though `p->decoders` still aliases caller-owned state and the function is about to return `NULL`.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this and the other interim error sites to `flb_interim_parser_destroy(p)`, which deliberately does not free `parser->decoders` or `parser->types` until ownership has actually transferred.

parser_admitted.description: After format setup and `time_fmt` duplication succeed, the staged witness reaches the `time_offset` validation subpath inside `flb_parser_create()`. This is the last admitted branch before the failing cleanup path.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete heap object later freed and then read. When the witness sets the decoder flag, the harness allocates the 16-byte decoder-list head here and passes it to `flb_parser_create()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the staged 100-byte witness, byte 36 is odd, so the decoder branch executes, allocates `list`, populates one decoder and one rule, and passes that pointer into `flb_parser_create()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 100-byte witness is decoded into parser arguments: `format = logfmt`, a non-null `time_fmt`, an invalid non-null `time_offset`, and one decoder `mk_list`, then passed into `flb_parser_create()`.
Parser creation stores the caller-owned decoder list in `p->decoders`, later rejects the supplied `time_offset`, and unwinds with `flb_parser_destroy(p)` even though creation failed.
The create-time unwind reaches `parser->decoders` and frees the caller-owned decoder list head at line 761.
Because `flb_parser_create()` returned `NULL`, the harness takes its failure-cleanup branch and calls `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` again on the same pointer.
The second destroy starts iterating the already freed list head, so `mk_list_foreach_safe` performs the ASan-reported heap-use-after-free READ.

fine_trace.note: The exact staged 100-byte witness chooses `format = "logfmt"` (`data[0] = 0xff`), materializes a non-null 15-byte `time_fmt`, materializes the 15-byte `time_offset` string `"\xff              "`, omits `time_key` and `types`, and enables one decoder list. The harness then passes both the invalid `time_offset` string and the allocated `list` pointer into `flb_parser_create()`.

Source. Before parser creation has succeeded, the function stores the caller-owned decoder-list pointer from step 0 into `p->decoders`. That makes the later generic parser destructor capable of freeing caller-owned state.

Because step 0 supplied non-null `time_fmt`, execution enters the `if (time_fmt)` block and later the `if (time_offset)` sub-block. `time_offset` is `"\xff              "`, so `flb_parser_tzone_offset()` returns `-1` immediately because the first byte is neither `Z`, `+`, nor `-`.

Root cause. On this create-time error path, vulnerable code calls the full `flb_parser_destroy(p)` even though `p->decoders` still aliases caller-owned `list` from step 1 and the function is returning `NULL`. The fix swaps this for `flb_interim_parser_destroy(p)` so the caller retains responsibility for `decoders` and `types` on failure.

The `flb_parser_destroy(p)` call from step 3 reaches `parser->decoders`, enters `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy()`, and finally frees the 16-byte decoder-list head itself here. This is the free recorded in ASan's free stack.

Since step 3 returned `NULL`, `fuzz_parser == NULL` and the harness takes its failure-cleanup branch. `list` still holds the same non-null address from step 0, so the caller assumes it still owns the decoder list and destroys it a second time.

fine_trace.note: Sink. The second destroy from step 5 starts iterating `list` after step 4 already freed that 16-byte list head. `mk_list_foreach_safe` therefore reads stale `next`/`prev` pointers from freed memory, matching the staged ASan heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 at line 743.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: n/a: the lifetime bug is caused by a premature free on create failure; the allocation itself occurs earlier in the harness.

format.name: parser_fuzzer input blob
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly 100 bytes. Its control bytes make `parser_fuzzer` choose `format = "logfmt"`, create a non-null 15-byte `time_fmt`, omit `time_key`, create a non-null 15-byte `time_offset` equal to `"\xff              "`, omit `types`, and allocate one decoder `mk_list` with one rule. That exact combination forces `flb_parser_create()` to validate the invalid `time_offset`, return `NULL` after freeing `list` through `flb_parser_destroy(p)`, and then the harness failure-cleanup path immediately call `flb_parser_decoder_list_destroy(list)` again on the same pointer.
